Nothing X App
The Nothing X App is a versatile mobile application available on both Android and iOS platforms, specifically designed to enhance user interaction and functionality across a range of Nothing audio devices, such as the Ear (open), Ear (a), Ear (2), and CMF earbuds. It provides a comprehensive suite of controls and customization options, including managing settings for active noise cancellation (ANC), equalizer adjustments, gesture controls, and dual connection functionalities. Users can also activate the Voice Assistant and personalize their audio experience through custom sound settings, bass adjustments, and Bluetooth codec options.

Available via the Google Play Store and iOS App Store, the Nothing X App enables firmware updates and synchronization for connected devices, ensuring they are always up-to-date. Additionally, it facilitates the management of notifications and device connections via Bluetooth, supporting seamless integration with mobile devices. The app serves as the official platform for managing various functionalities, allowing users to customize settings and manage features across several Nothing products, including earbuds and Buds Pro. Whether it is adjusting audio quality or configuring device functionalities, the Nothing X App provides users with robust controls to tailor their listening experience.

iOS
iOS is a mobile operating system used by devices compatible with the CMF Watch app for the Watch Pro.<SEP>iOS is an operating system used by Apple mobile devices, which provides a platform for using apps including the Nothing X App.

Ear (open)
Ear (open) are innovative wireless earbuds developed by Nothing, known for their unique ear-hook design and functionality. These earbuds offer gesture controls that allow users to manage functions like volume and noise cancellation, contingent upon device compatibility, although they do not support active noise cancellation (ANC). Featuring Bluetooth 5.3, they support Google Fast Pair, Microsoft Swift Pair, and Dual Connection capabilities, allowing seamless connectivity and automatic reconnection to the last paired device under specific conditions. Ear (open) are also equipped with IP54 water and dust resistance, custom EQ settings, and are designed to provide stability during outdoor activities. Compatible with Android 5.1 and above and iOS 13 and higher, they ensure wide usability across various devices. Recognized for their sound quality through user experiences, these earbuds can be managed using apps like the Nothing X App for enhanced control and personalization.

Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)
Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) is a wireless communication protocol used by the Nothing X App to connect with devices while conserving power, though communication is paused during calls.

Android
Android is a widely used mobile operating system referenced in various contexts for app management and device connectivity. It is utilized by devices compatible with applications such as the Nothing X App, which manages device connections and requires specific permission settings to function effectively. Additionally, Android supports the CMF Watch app for the Watch Pro and is compatible with the Ear (stick) through Bluetooth integration, with version 5.0+ facilitating this connection. This operating system is further mentioned in scenarios related to confirming connections between devices, such as the Nothing Phone, and is integral to data transfer processes to this specific phone. Android serves as the primary operating system across a multitude of smartphones, supporting a range of applications and hardware functionalities.

Nothing Ear
Nothing Ear is a line of advanced wireless earbuds produced by Nothing Technology Limited, designed to integrate seamlessly with the Nothing Phone and other mobile devices. These earbuds boast a variety of cutting-edge audio technologies, including Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) and Dual Connection capabilities, allowing users to pair them with multiple devices simultaneously, up to eight connections. Bluetooth 5.3 support ensures efficient connectivity, while features like wireless and fast charging add to their convenience. The earbuds stand out with specific audio settings such as AAC mode to optimize battery life, custom EQ settings for tailored sound experiences, and Fast Pair connectivity for effortless pairing. Furthermore, the Nothing Ear can be managed through apps like the Nothing X App, enhancing user control over their listening experience. This product line showcases Nothing's commitment to delivering premium, versatile audio devices that cater to modern technological needs.

CMF Watch
CMF Watch is an application mentioned as requiring certain start and lock procedures on Android devices for optimal performance.

Nothing Support Team
Nothing Support Team is a customer service entity offering assistance for persistent device issues with the Nothing Phone.<SEP>The Nothing Support Team is a customer service department that provides assistance for issues related to sound clarity during calls and signal stability.<SEP>The Nothing Support Team provides assistance for unresolved issues with applications and devices.

Customer Support
Customer Support is a vital service entity dedicated to assisting users with a wide range of technical and application-related issues. This service is provided by organizations, including the company Nothing, and is focused on helping customers resolve problems with their products and services. Customer Support offers comprehensive assistance for unresolved issues with devices and applications, particularly when troubleshooting steps have failed. The team is responsible for guiding users through the resolution of persistent issues, including but not limited to, restoring devices to factory defaults, resetting passwords, and addressing technical concerns such as phone charging, sound, and overall functionality. They are also available to answer queries related to products like CMF earbuds and Nothing devices, ensuring that customers receive necessary support for phone and device operations. Customer Support is accessible for additional help, equipped to provide solutions for any technical inquiries or troubleshooting needs related to smartphone and application usage.

VPN
VPN, or Virtual Private Network, is mentioned as a factor that could affect network connectivity and internet speed.

SIM Card
A SIM Card, or Subscriber Identification Module, is a critical component used in mobile devices, including smartphones such as the Nothing Phone, for network connectivity and cellular services. It is a removable, portable smart card designed to store user data and network authorization information, such as the phone number and carrier details, enabling the device to access various wireless services. SIM cards are essential for connecting mobile devices to cellular networks, supporting data and call functions, and facilitating network connectivity during the setup of new phones. They play a crucial role in managing communication functions and can be tested in different devices to address internet speed issues. SIM cards are often involved in the data transfer process and are necessary for network connectivity and phone operation. The Nothing Phone supports dual SIM capabilities, allowing the user flexibility in network connectivity, including dual 4G modes. Overall, SIM cards are indispensable for accessing mobile network information and managing data use and connectivity for seamless mobile communication.

Browser
A Browser is a software application used to access information on the World Wide Web.<SEP>A browser is a software application used to access and navigate the internet, offering features like clearing browsing data.<SEP>Browser is a device application that allows users to access internet sites and manage their browsing history and data.<SEP>The browser is an application type that might freeze and has specific instructions for troubleshooting.

App
An app, or application, is software that may experience various functional issues, requiring troubleshooting.

Multi-task Management Interface
The Multi-task Management Interface on Android devices is used to manage running applications, such as locking apps for performance.

Google Play Store
The Google Play Store is a comprehensive digital distribution platform operated by Google, specifically designed for Android devices. It serves as the primary marketplace for users to browse, download, and update a wide range of applications, games, and other digital content. Notable applications available through the Google Play Store include the Nothing X App, CMF Watch app, and ChatGPT, among many others, serving various devices such as the Nothing Phone and Nothing Ear. This platform is essential for Android users, providing the latest versions of applications and ensuring that users can easily transfer or download apps that may not have been established during initial data setups. With its vast collection of apps and seamless user experience, the Google Play Store is integral to the Android ecosystem, facilitating access to numerous digital utilities and entertainment options.

Settings
Settings refer to the configuration options available across various smart devices, including smartphones like the Nothing Phone and wearable technology such as the Watch Pro. As the main interface on a device, Settings enable users to access, customize, and manage different system options and features for optimal device performance and personalized user experience. On the Nothing Phone, the Settings menu allows users to adjust preferences and configurations, including display, security, connectivity, notification preferences, and privacy features. Users can manage functions such as network, internet, SIM card, and data preferences, as well as specific features like game mode and device connectivity. Similarly, on the Watch Pro, the Settings menu provides access to options for adjusting display settings, conducting a factory reset, and managing associated apps for comprehensive device control. Overall, Settings serve as an essential control panel that facilitates the customization and management of device functionalities, permissions, and system operations, whether it's adjusting volume, updating software, configuring Google services, or handling app management.

Nothing X app
The Nothing X app is a versatile mobile application available on both Android and iOS platforms, designed to manage and enhance the functionality of Nothing-branded audio devices. Users can utilize the app to connect, update, and customize settings for a variety of earbuds, including the Ear (1), Ear (stick), CMF Buds Pro 2, Neckband Pro, and Ear (a). The app provides access to a range of features such as firmware updates, gesture controls, and Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) settings. It enables users to configure equalizer settings, Smart Dial configurations, control gestures, and wake up the voice assistant. Moreover, the Nothing X app offers Bluetooth audio encoding customization and provides a platform for personalized user experience by tailoring device functionalities to individual preferences. This application is readily accessible via the Google Play Store and iOS App Store, making it an essential tool for users seeking to optimize the performance and utility of their Nothing earbuds.

Bluetooth Audio Codec
Bluetooth Audio Codec refers to the method of encoding audio for transmission over Bluetooth, with AAC being a common choice for quality streaming.

Microphone
Microphone refers to the hardware and related permissions required for audio input on mobile apps and devices.

Network Connection
Network Connection denotes the linking of devices to the internet via WiFi or mobile data to enable app functionality and updates.<SEP>Network connection failures during a call can be caused by congestion, SIM card issues, or network conditions.

WiFi
WiFi is a versatile wireless networking technology that enables devices to connect to the internet or communicate with one another within a specific area. This technology is based on the IEEE 802.11 standards and plays a crucial role in wireless local area networking. WiFi uses radio waves to facilitate high-speed internet and network connections, making it essential for setting up and transferring data between devices, such as phones. It is also commonly referenced in airplane mode settings, demonstrating its ubiquity in modern electronic devices. Additionally, WiFi is a key technology utilized by devices like the Nothing Phone to establish internet connectivity.

Developer Options
Developer Options are settings in a device's system that allow advanced configurations, including USB debugging.<SEP>Developer Options is a menu in Android devices that provides additional features for developers and advanced users to customize and troubleshoot the system.<SEP>Developer Options is a section in Android settings allowing advanced configuration and features for developers, like USB Debugging.

App Cache
App Cache refers to the temporary storage used by apps to store frequently accessed data for quick retrieval, which can be cleared to resolve issues.

CMF Buds Pro 2
The CMF Buds Pro 2 are advanced wireless earbuds created by Nothing, designed with a multitude of sophisticated features catering to diverse audio needs. Prominent features include Active Noise Cancellation (ANC), capable of reducing noise levels by up to 50dB, allowing for a customizable listening experience via the Nothing X App. These earbuds offer a dual connection mode, enabling seamless connectivity to multiple devices, with the capability for auto-reconnection under certain conditions. Users can enjoy various audio enhancements such as spatial audio effects and multiple equalizer presets. 

The CMF Buds Pro 2 are compatible with both Android and iOS devices, featuring robust protection against dust and sweat, making them suitable for diverse environments and activities. The design includes intuitive touch controls for easy management of music playback, volume adjustments, and ANC settings. However, some users have reported issues with rapid battery drain attributed to high volume settings and specific codec usage. Additionally, these earbuds support fast charging, ensuring minimal downtime between uses. Overall, the CMF Buds Pro 2 provide a comprehensive and adaptable audio experience enhanced by modern technological advancements.

Nothing Ear (1)
Nothing Ear (1) is a model of earbuds designed to optimize audio performance through configurations like AAC mode to enhance battery life and connectivity.<SEP>Nothing Ear (1) is a wireless earbud offering various features such as ANC modes, Bluetooth capabilities, and compatibility with the Nothing X app.

iOS App Store
The iOS App Store is Apple's digital distribution platform designed for iOS devices, where users can download applications, games, and other content. Among the various apps available, the Nothing X App is offered for download on this platform. This app allows users to configure and manage features related to the Nothing Ear (open) and Buds, providing functionality for controlling their settings. The iOS App Store facilitates the downloading and updating of the Nothing X App for users seeking to enhance their audio experience with Nothing devices.

AAC Mode
AAC Mode refers to an audio codec setting available on Nothing Ear earbuds that can improve battery performance during audio playback.

Bluetooth Device
A Bluetooth Device is a technical term referencing smartphones, tablets, or laptops that can connect wirelessly to Nothing earphones for audio streaming.

Battery Life
Battery Life refers to the duration for which various devices can operate between charges, influenced by usage scenarios, audio settings, and other conditions. Specifically, the Buds Pro Earbuds can provide up to 11 hours of continuous music playback, with variations depending on ANC settings and modes of operation. Similarly, the Ear (a) performance changes with modes such as ANC ON or OFF. The CMF Buds Pro 2 offer differences in playback and talk time based on usage conditions, while the CMF Buds 2 are noted for extensive usage durations under various modes, detailing active usage and standby times contingent on the features engaged. For smartwatches, the Battery Life of the Watch Pro and Watch Pro 2 varies by usage intensity, from typical to heavy use. Furthermore, Battery Life can be maintained or extended through practices like regular charging, maintaining proper temperature, and avoiding overuse during charging, enhancing the operational duration across different devices including the Nothing earphones and Nothing Ear (open), with operational times differing greatly between music playback and communication scenarios.

Nothing Customer Service
Customer support service for Nothing device users to address concerns and provide solutions for audio device problems.<SEP>Nothing Customer Service is tasked with offering support and replacements for products of the brand Nothing, specifically for charging issues with cases and earbuds.<SEP>Nothing Customer Service is the support service for Nothing products, assisting customers with troubleshooting and inquiries.<SEP>Nothing Customer Service provides support and assistance for users of Nothing's devices, including the Ear (2).<SEP>Nothing Customer Service provides support and assistance to users of Nothing products, including the Nothing Ear.

Nothing OS
Nothing OS serves as the operating system for various devices in the Nothing brand, including Nothing Phone (1) and Nothing Phone (2a), and is also integrated with accessories like the Ear (a) earbuds and Ear (2). It is based on Android 14, providing a robust software platform that supports interface and feature customizations. Starting from version 1.1.4, Nothing OS offers integration of the Nothing X app in Device Details, alongside enhanced customization options for both phones and earbuds. Notably, Nothing OS facilities software updates to improve functionality and user experience across Nothing devices.

Bluetooth
Bluetooth is a wireless technology standard that facilitates the exchange of data and communication over short distances between both fixed and mobile devices. This technology is commonly utilized to create personal area networks, allowing seamless connectivity and interaction among a variety of devices, including electronic gadgets like CMF Earbuds, Ear (stick), Ear (1) earbuds, phones, laptops, Watch Pro, and other compatible devices. Bluetooth technology is especially important for ensuring wireless pairing and connectivity, with a typical range of up to 10 meters, enabling devices such as the Watch Pro to make and receive calls once paired with smartphones. Additionally, Bluetooth is often referenced in relation to airplane mode settings and connection issues with different devices. Its functionality extends beyond basic data transfer, offering capabilities for information sharing, updates, device syncing, and management, thereby playing a crucial role in modern wireless communication solutions.

Ear (2)
Ear (2) is a model of wireless earbuds produced by Nothing, known for their advanced features and connectivity.<SEP>Ear (2) is a pair of wireless earbuds featuring specifications such as dual connection capability, active noise cancellation, ENC, and various audio support functions like Google Fast Pair and LDAC.<SEP>Ear (2) is a set of advanced Bluetooth-enabled earbuds designed by Nothing, featuring Dual Connection capabilities, customizable gesture controls, noise cancellation, and options for personalized sound profiles.

Ear (a)
Ear (a) are earbuds that offer various features such as Active Noise Cancellation, fast-charging, Dual Connection, and are water/dust resistant.<SEP>Ear (a) are wireless earbuds that include features such as high-definition audio streaming, gesture controls, dual connection functionality, noise cancellation, and integration with the Nothing X App.<SEP>Ear (a) is a brand of earbuds that supports custom EQ settings and various sound effects, designed to provide high-quality audio experiences for music enthusiasts.<SEP>Ear (a) is a model of wireless earbuds produced by Nothing, mentioned in relation to connection and reconnection processes.

Watch Pro
The Watch Pro is a versatile and multifunctional smartwatch designed to cater to a wide range of user needs. It boasts a 340 mAh battery and is equipped with a 1.96-inch AMOLED display, providing a clear and vibrant interface. Watch Pro supports Bluetooth calling and connects to mobile devices via Bluetooth, enabling convenient call and message notifications. Additionally, it offers customizable watch faces and features for exercise and fitness tracking, including monitoring of heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep patterns, stress, and step count. Built with various sensors and algorithms for high accuracy, the Watch Pro is ideal for monitoring health metrics.

For added functionality, Watch Pro utilizes the CMF Watch app, which allows for display settings, music control, phone tracking, weather updates, and firmware upgrades. Users can pair the device with other tech gadgets for enriched connectivity. While the smartwatch supports a vast range of sports activities and offers customizable exercise types, it does not include NFC or eSIM capabilities. Furthermore, Watch Pro features interchangeable straps and IP68 dust and water resistance, making it a durable option for active lifestyles.

The device's ability to synchronize with the CMF Watch app is crucial for optimal performance, allowing time syncing and access to additional features such as contact list integration for displaying caller names or numbers. When specific connection issues arise, troubleshooting may be necessary to ensure seamless operation with iOS devices and other compatible smartphones. Overall, the Watch Pro stands out as a powerful accessory, merging fitness tracking with communication capabilities in a sleek wearable package.

CMF Watch app
The CMF Watch app is a versatile mobile application developed to enhance and manage the functionalities of the Watch Pro and Watch Pro 2 devices. It serves as a companion tool, allowing users to connect their smartwatch to a smartphone for seamless integration and improved performance. The app facilitates customization, enabling users to manage watch faces, exercise settings, and notification preferences. Additionally, it supports health data syncing and camera remote control, providing a comprehensive smartwatch experience. Users can benefit from device upgrades, including firmware updates and volume adjustments for optimal functionality. The CMF Watch app also expands language support and manages contact lists, ensuring effective communication by displaying caller information. Through the app, users can access weather updates and other features, making it an essential tool for enhancing their smartwatch capabilities.

CMF Watch App
The CMF Watch App is a mobile software application designed to pair with smartwatches, specifically the Watch Pro and Watch Pro 2, to provide enhanced user experience and functionalities. It offers a comprehensive suite of features, including managing notifications, settings customization, syncing data, upgrading firmware, and troubleshooting device issues. Additionally, the app supports tasks such as time synchronization and monitoring, and provides additional features for tracking and managing fitness activities. Users are encouraged to download the CMF Watch App to fully configure and enjoy the varied functionalities of the Watch Pro and Watch Pro 2.

CMF Watch Pro
CMF Watch Pro is a smartwatch that connects to devices via Bluetooth, requiring troubleshooting steps for connectivity issues.

Phone
A phone, possibly a smartphone, that interacts with earbuds and may experience Bluetooth connectivity issues.<SEP>Phone is a mobile communication device that connects to CMF Earbuds via Bluetooth for audio output and calls.<SEP>Phone refers to mobile devices generally discussed in the context of settings, maintenance, and data transfer.<SEP>The Phone is a device referenced throughout the text for functions like battery management, file restoration, and location services.

Charging Case
The Charging Case is an essential device enclosure designed for charging and storing earbuds, such as CMF Earbuds, Ear (a) earbuds, and Buds Pro. It plays a crucial role in providing additional battery life and enabling portable charging, ensuring that earbuds remain powered when not in use. Users may utilize the Charging Case for various functions, including facilitating hard resets or factory resets, which can improve the earbuds' connection to other devices. To ensure optimal performance, it is important for users to maintain clean ports and undamaged cables, as these factors can influence connectivity and charging efficiency.

Specifically designed for Buds Pro, the Charging Case features a notable battery capacity of 460mAh and an IPX2 rating, indicating a level of water resistance suited for everyday use. The Charging Case for CMF Buds Pro 2 offers advanced power management capabilities and boasts a rubber paint finish that enhances its aesthetic appeal. Overall, the Charging Case serves as a crucial component in managing earbuds' power and connectivity, requiring proper handling and maintenance to deliver effective results.

Phone Call Audio

CMF earbuds
CMF earbuds are Bluetooth-enabled earphones with dual connection capabilities, gesture controls, and compatibility with the Nothing X app.<SEP>CMF earbuds are audio devices with sound quality based on user experiences, customizable through the Nothing X App.

Android device

Google Play

Specifically, it offers the Nothing X app, which can be utilized to manage settings for Nothing Ear devices and Buds. As the primary store for Android apps, Google Play facilitates a variety of app downloads, including the Nothing X app, effectively supporting users in customizing their audio accessories.

App Store

Among the apps available for download are the Nothing X app and the CMF Watch app. This service facilitates iOS users in accessing a plethora of applications, ensuring seamless integration and functionality with their devices.

Voice Assistant
The Voice Assistant is a versatile digital assistant feature that can be activated and controlled through the Nothing X app. It is designed to enhance user interaction with various devices, such as the Nothing Ear (open), CMF earbuds, and CMF Buds Pro 2, by facilitating voice commands for hands-free operation. Users can engage with the Voice Assistant via gestures set in the app, allowing seamless access to virtual assistant functions on devices like Ear (a) and Buds. This feature provides users with the convenience and efficiency of interacting with their devices through simple voice commands, enhancing the overall user experience without the need for manual control.

LDAC
LDAC is a high-definition audio codec supported by Ear (2) that allows streaming of high-resolution audio at high transmission bit rates.<SEP>LDAC is a high-definition audio codec supported by Ear (a), enabling high-resolution audio streaming at 990kbps.<SEP>LDAC is a high-definition audio codec used for improving audio quality over Bluetooth connections.<SEP>LDAC is an audio codec provided by Nothing Ear, known for transmitting high-resolution audio.<SEP>LDAC is an audio coding technology allowing high-resolution audio transmission over Bluetooth, enhancing sound quality.

Gesture Controls allow users to manage audio playback, call handling, and other functions on the Ear (2) earbuds.<SEP>Gesture Controls refer to the touch-based operations on CMF Earbuds that allow users to play/pause audio, control calls, and activate other features through gestures.

Dual Connection Feature
Dual Connection Feature allows the CMF Earbuds to connect with two devices simultaneously via Bluetooth.<SEP>The dual connection feature allows CMF Buds Pro 2 to connect to two devices simultaneously, offering flexibility in device usage.

Nothing Technology

Classic Bluetooth

AAC
AAC is a Bluetooth codec supported by Ear (a), used commonly across various devices for audio transmission.<SEP>AAC is an audio codec supported by iOS devices for high-quality audio streaming over Bluetooth.<SEP>AAC is an audio coding format that provides high-quality digital audio sound, supported by the earbuds.<SEP>AAC is an audio format supported by Nothing Ear, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of devices.

High-Quality Audio
High-Quality Audio refers to the superior audio performance achieved through codecs like LDAC and AAC.

Active Noise Cancellation
Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) is a feature that reduces unwanted ambient sounds using active noise control on the CMF Buds Pro 2.<SEP>Active Noise Cancellation is a feature in Buds Pro that reduces ambient sound, enhancing the listening experience.<SEP>Active Noise Cancellation is a mode on Ear (a) that reduces ambient noise for clearer listening.<SEP>Active Noise Cancellation is a mode on the Buds that minimizes ambient noise for an enhanced audio experience.

Transparency Mode
Transparency Mode is a feature found in various audio devices, such as Ear (a), Neckband Pro, Buds, and CMF Buds Pro 2. This feature enhances user awareness of their surroundings by allowing ambient sounds to be heard alongside audio playback. It simulates the effect of not wearing earbuds, enabling users to maintain situational awareness while listening to audio. Transparency Mode provides the ability to hear external sounds, making it particularly useful for maintaining awareness in different environments.

Touch Controls
Touch Controls are interactive features on CMF Buds Pro 2, allowing users to manage playback, calls, and other settings with finger gestures.

CMF
CMF is the organization that produces the CMF Buds Pro 2 and provides customer support for its products.

Spatial Audio Effect
Spatial Audio Effect enhances audio experience by utilizing the Head-Related Transfer Function model.<SEP>Spatial Audio Effect in CMF Buds Pro 2 uses the Head-Related Transfer Function model to create a 3D immersive sound experience.<SEP>Spatial Audio Effect is a feature in the Neckband Pro that creates an immersive 3D sound experience using the HRTF model.<SEP>Spatial Audio Effect is a feature providing a 3D cinematic-grade sound experience based on the Head-Related Transfer Function model.

Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF)
HRTF is a model used in audio engineering to emulate how sound reaches the ear from different points in space, aiding in the creation of spatial audio effects.

Smart ANC Algorithm
The Smart ANC Algorithm is an advanced noise cancellation technology that adjusts parameters based on environmental noise levels to optimize user experience.<SEP>The Smart ANC Algorithm is used by Ear (a) to provide adaptive active noise cancellation depending on the environmental noise level.

Plastic Casing
High-quality plastic casing is used in CMF Buds Pro 2 for durability, UV resistance, and impact resistance.

Silicone Ear Tips
Silicone ear tips are designed for comfortable and secure fitting in the CMF Buds Pro 2.<SEP>Silicone ear tips enhance the comfort and fit of Ear (a) earbuds.

Bluetooth 5.3
Bluetooth 5.3 is a wireless technology standard that facilitates efficient and seamless connectivity between devices. This version of Bluetooth technology is utilized by various products, including Ear (a), Nothing Ear, Watch Pro, Buds Pro, Buds, CMF Buds Pro 2, and Neckband Pro. Each of these devices benefits from the improved connectivity and performance offered by Bluetooth 5.3, enhancing their ability to communicate wirelessly with other devices. This version is particularly noted for its advanced capabilities in maintaining strong, stable connections across multiple device interactions.

IP55 Protection Rating

DIRAC OPTEO

LDAC, AAC, SBC
LDAC, AAC, and SBC are audio formats supported by CMF Buds Pro 2, offering varied audio quality parameters.

Smart Dial
Smart Dial is a customizable control feature on the charging case that supports various functions such as volume control and noise cancellation.<SEP>The Smart Dial is a control mechanism on the Neckband Pro, allowing for various actions such as adjusting volume, switching noise cancellation modes, and controlling music playback.

Ultra Bass Technology
Ultra Bass Technology enhances low-frequency signals in music for a more dynamic bass experience.<SEP>Ultra Bass Technology enhances low-frequency sounds in real-time, providing dynamic audio enhancement for the Buds Pro earbuds.<SEP>Ultra Bass Technology in the Buds enhances low-frequency signals dynamically, providing an enhanced bass experience adjustable through the Nothing X app.<SEP>Ultra Bass Technology is a sound enhancement feature in the Neckband Pro that improves the perception of low-frequency signals in music.

Adaptive Mode
Adaptive Mode in Ear (a) adjusts noise cancellation levels based on environmental noise.<SEP>Adaptive Mode is a noise control feature that adjusts noise cancellation based on environmental sound levels.

Active Noise Cancellation (ANC)
ANC is a technology used in Nothing Ear that reduces unwanted ambient sounds using active noise control.<SEP>Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) is a feature of CMF Buds 2 supporting noise reduction up to 48dB, enhancing user listening experience by eliminating ambient sounds.<SEP>Active Noise Cancellation is a feature in earbuds designed to reduce unwanted ambient sounds using active noise control.

Dual Connection
Dual Connection is a versatile feature available in various Nothing Ear earbuds, including models such as Ear (open), Ear (a), and Ear (2). This functionality allows the earbuds to connect simultaneously to two Bluetooth devices, enabling seamless management of audio playback and call audio priorities based on user activity. The feature enhances flexibility by allowing easy switching between devices and managing calls and audio playback seamlessly. Some earbuds, like CMF Buds 2, also support this feature, giving users the ability to connect to two different devices simultaneously, although users may occasionally experience sound output delays. Overall, Dual Connection provides users with the capability to stay connected across multiple devices, ensuring convenience and efficiency in handling audio functions.

Fast Charging
Fast Charging capability of Nothing Ear (open) allows the earbuds to power up quickly, offering extended use with a short charging time.<SEP>Fast Charging in Ear (2) allows rapid power restore, enabling significant usage time after a short charge period.<SEP>Fast Charging is a feature available in CMF Buds 2, enabling quick recharge to provide extended usage time, notably providing 4-hour usage with a 10-minute charge without ANC.<SEP>Fast Charging is a feature of Ear (a) allowing quick charging, enabling extended usage with short charging durations.<SEP>Fast Charging is a feature of the Buds Pro Earbuds, allowing for quick recharge, providing 3 hours of use with a 10-minute charge.

CMF Buds 2
CMF Buds 2 are wireless earbuds offering features like Active Noise Cancellation, Spatial Audio Effect, and dual device connection, made with durable materials such as a high-quality plastic casing and silicone ear tips.

Dirac Opteo
Dirac Opteo is a default audio tuning option provided by the collaboration between CMF by Nothing and Dirac.<SEP>Dirac Opteo is a sound enhancement technology incorporated in the Buds to optimize audio output and maximize acoustic performance using patented correction technology.<SEP>Dirac Opteo is a sound optimization technology used in CMF Buds 2 for enhancing audio output by correcting sound resonances and colorations digitally.

Bluetooth 5.4
